task: etcd and all nfs-csi PVs shared master-1's one VMDK; an NFS write burst stalled etcd WAL fsync (>8s), the apiserver timed out and CNPG restarted and failed over. Put the NFS export on its own virtual disk, make CNPG tolerant of a stall (liveness, resources), and fix the CNPG monitoring target database that does not exist.

events.summary: Change only: the Vagrantfile second disk for master-1 plus NFS_DATA_DEVICE=auto, its resolution in 01-nfs-server.sh, CNPG probes/resources/bootstrap database in narwhal-db.yaml and 07-cnpg.sh, the operations.md migration and host-load sections, R327. Deliberately left alone: the live cluster and VMs (read-only kubectl plus one server-side dry-run that persists nothing), failoverDelay, Postgres parameters, Kakao NFS volume path, the existing nfs-xfs-migration runbook, authentik-db-rw ExternalName Service, prometheus-alerts.yaml.

Read-only live checks 2026-11-08: narwhal-db spec.resources is {} (BestEffort); probes.liveness is the default (failureThreshold 3, period 10, isolationCheck 1000ms); psql -l lists gitea, harbor, keycloak, narwhal, postgres and no authentik, while spec.bootstrap.initdb.database is authentik and the instance log shows the cnpg_metrics_exporter failing to connect to database authentik. git log -S: gitops/resources/narwhal-db.yaml kept authentik from 94b72c37; a301deb1 changed the scripts only. The shared-VMDK incident facts (17 PVs, etcd fsync >8s) come from the incident report, not re-measured here.

D-NFS-VMDK: config.vm.disk nfs-data on master-1 (vmware_desktop plugin 3.0.5 disk capability: growable vmdk; bus set to nvme via vmware_desktop__bus_type to match the box's nvme0 OS disk, because the plugin default is scsi/lsilogic and scsi0.present is FALSE on arm64 Fusion) and NFS_DATA_DEVICE=auto, resolved to exactly one blank non-OS disk, fstab by UUID, existing refusal to mount over live data kept. D-CNPG-RESTART-AMP: probes.liveness 12 x 10s, timeout 10s, isolationCheck 5s, readiness default. D-CNPG-RESOURCES: requests 512Mi/250m, memory limit 1Gi, no CPU limit (CFS throttling would delay /healthz). D-NFS-VMDK-GUARD: the Vagrantfile aborts NARWHAL_NFS_DISK_GB=0 once master-1 has recorded nfs-data, because vagrant-vmware-desktop 3.0.5 cleanup_disks deletes (vmware-vdiskmanager -U) a disk missing from the config; the guard was exercised with plain ruby on the extracted lines (refuse, override passes, 200 passes), not through vagrant. D-CNPG-APPDB: bootstrap database/owner narwhal in narwhal-db.yaml so the default monitoring queries target an existing database. operations.md section 15 (owner-run migration incl. XFS project-ID restore) and 16 (host load).

events.scope: Static: R327 parses the Vagrantfile, 01-nfs-server.sh, the narwhal-db.yaml Cluster and the 07-cnpg.sh heredoc Cluster and rejects 17 single-defect mutations; ruby -c Vagrantfile; bash -n on both scripts; a server-side dry-run of the new Cluster manifest against the live CNPG webhook and CRD was accepted (nothing persisted). NOT covered: the NVMe attach on a real VM (unverified until the owner-run migration step 4), a real vagrant up with the second disk, the auto resolver on a real guest, the rsync migration and quota restore, the instance rolling restart, whether the longer liveness actually prevents a restart in a stall, any etcd fsync improvement.

events.summary: In the repository a fresh cluster gets a separate NFS disk and a stall-tolerant CNPG cluster whose monitoring target exists, pinned by R327, and the existing-cluster migration is documented as an owner-run runbook. Nothing is deployed: the live cluster still shares one VMDK, the bootstrap-database and probe changes reach it only when 14-gitops-bootstrap.sh next applies narwhal-db.yaml by kubectl apply (no Argo Application owns the Cluster; the apply rolls both instances, primary restarting in place), and the same-host-SSD limit means the etcd benefit is unmeasured.
Complete for the repository scope; not deployed, migration not run, the quota-limit re-application after rsync is unverified.
